notes: PR1 «seq/ETag save sequencing» (v1.11.67) — the last approved item of the grouped audit (bug-hunt B-05 = full-audit PR1). PROBLEM: daysDone was not in _MERGED_STATE_KEYS, so a partial POST /api/state whole-replaced daysDone and every other non-merged key (usefulMinutes, timerSessions, custom_boxes, deleted, assignments, testLog, errorLog, sleepLog/sleepReminded/lastErrorReview, examTargets/classLinks, telegramChatId) — live-confirmed in the audit: POST {"daysDone": {}} wiped the flag. A naive key-level merge was not the fix: the frontend genuinely DELETES entries from those keys, and a merge would resurrect deletions. PROTOCOL (user-chosen 27 Nov 05:20, «seq/ETag رو انتخاب می‌کنم»): the server assigns a monotonic sequence per save, persisted in seq.json in the data dir (one counter for state, one for testbook), bumped exactly once per persisted change inside save_state/save_testbook — so box create/update/delete, pull absorbs, the Telegram-token save and restores/recovery/migration writes all move the counter. Every client save sends the last-seen seq: X-State-Seq / X-Testbook-Seq + X-State-Full / X-Testbook-Full headers on fetch, _seq / _full / _beacon in the JSON body on sendBeacon (which cannot set headers). GET /api/state and /api/testbook return the current seq in the X-State-Seq / X-Testbook-Seq response header; POST responses return the new seq the same way; the POST /api/state body stays exactly {"ok": true} (L-PERF8). STALE-WRITE BEHAVIOUR: a full save whose seq is behind the server's is REJECTED with HTTP 409 carrying {error, seq, state/testbook} — the client silently rebases its own changes onto the server state (3-way merge against its last-synced snapshot: per-entry for dicts, per-element by id for arrays, merged keys take mine because the retry POST goes through the server's per-box deep merge, activeTimer whole-object with the PR3 startedAt guard still applying) and retries, max 3 attempts, with no toast on a 409 itself (the ب-۷ error toast with retry only fires when the retries are exhausted or the server answers another error). A genuine deletion is never resurrected by the rebase: the rebase only takes the server's value for a key/entry the client did NOT touch since its last sync. A stale BEACON (pagehide, no response readable) falls back to a PATCH merge — merged keys + activeTimer guards + scalar values only — so the closing tab's ticks survive while its day-flags/useful changes are dropped rather than clobbering the newer save. A PARTIAL POST is patched the same way: only the merged keys (done, tests, edits, actualMinutes, tests_total) + the activeTimer guards + scalar values are applied; every dict/list-valued non-merged key present is ignored — the audit repro POST {"daysDone": {}} no longer wipes the flag. Scalars are exempt on purpose: a scalar has no entries to wipe, so a partial scalar update is a genuine new value (this is what the 1.11.64 telegramChatId live tests pin — a partial {"telegramChatId": "abc!!"} still applies and is sanitized). A FULL save is a client-marked _full save, or a body carrying at least 90% of the DEFAULT_STATE keys (a whole-state save may omit a few server-managed keys — the drivers' GOOD_STATE fixture omits version / programme_start / programme_end — and is still full). A FULL save with a current seq applies authoritatively (present non-merged keys replace), so a genuine daysDone deletion in a full body still applies. TESTBOOK: a seq-matched full save REPLACES the testbook wholesale (no book-level merge) — the 1.11.61 caveat is RESOLVED by the seq protocol, not left as a comment: a deliberately deleted book is never resurrected. A legacy testbook save (no _full marker) keeps the 1.11.61 book-level merge, and a stale beacon falls back to it (safe: no book-delete UI exists, so a book absent from a stale beacon body is a book added later, which the merge correctly preserves). LEGACY CLIENTS: a client without the _full marker (a tab open from before this update — its old per-tab counter is ignored) still works: a full body is applied as before, a partial body is patched; reload tabs open from before the update for the 409 protection. A client seq AHEAD of the server's (seq.json lost) is trusted and adopted (server := client+1). KNOWN LIMITS (unchanged from before, documented): same-box concurrent edits stay last-writer-wins; a purgeBoxState deletion of a done entry is still resurrected by the server's per-box deep merge (inert — the box is deleted). PROVEN by a two-tab jsdom harness (verify1167): tab A's save does not wipe tab B's daysDone flag and vice versa, stale-write rejection + rebase + retry, the beacon carrying the seq, the partial-POST probe, and the deleted-book non-resurrection check; plus in-repo tests (TestPR1_1167), a live-server driver and smoke. Nothing deferred. i18n 1439/1439 (no new keys — the 409 rebase is silent and reuses the existing ب-۷ toast).
